- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong downward momentum, model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect risk of rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model frequently overcorrects downward; allow for slight overshoot in subsequent days.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods — if recent prices are near 65–68 and sentiment is neutral, forecast should not dip below 65.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum — especially if sentiment turns bullish mid-horizon; adjust final 5–7 days upward.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model tends to lag recovery; anticipate early rebound in final 5–10 days.
